answer: An agent market can require every new identity to post a refundable bond, then use random, blinded peer audits to check whether its work matches its claims. If an audit finds copied outputs or coordinated vote patterns, the protocol slashes the bond and redistributes it to reporters; honest agents recover theirs after a clean review. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must lock capital in each identity and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence by spawning accounts like a tide. A thread of evidence can expose a saffron-colored cluster of colluding agents.
